glossary.Pulmonary arterial pressure: Blood pressure inside the pulmonary arteries that carry blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.
glossary.Right heart failure: Failure of the right ventricle to pump blood forward, so blood backs up into the veins causing oedema and raised JVP.
glossary.Right heart strain: Overwork of the right ventricle against high pressure, seen on ECG and echo before it fails.
glossary.Interstitial lung disease: A group of conditions that scar and stiffen the tissue between the air sacs of the lungs.
glossary.Congenital heart disease: A structural heart problem present from birth, such as a hole between heart chambers.
glossary.PE: Pulmonary embolism: a blood clot, usually from the leg veins, that lodges in the lung arteries.
glossary.Pulmonary embolism: A blood clot, usually from the leg veins, that travels to and blocks a lung artery.
glossary.Chronic thromboembolic disease: Lung arteries left permanently narrowed by old clots that never dissolved.
glossary.Syncope: A brief loss of consciousness caused by a temporary drop in blood flow to the brain.
glossary.Arrhythmias: Abnormal heart rhythms, too fast, too slow or irregular.
glossary.S2: The second heart sound, made by the aortic and pulmonary valves closing at the end of systole.
glossary.Loud P2: A loud pulmonary valve closure sound, because high pulmonary pressure snaps the valve shut.
glossary.Diastolic: Happening while the heart muscle relaxes and the chambers fill.
glossary.Murmur: An extra heart sound caused by turbulent blood flow through a valve or defect.
glossary.Peaked P waves: Tall, pointed P waves on ECG showing an enlarged right atrium.
glossary.Right atrium: The heart chamber that receives blood from the body before passing it to the right ventricle.
glossary.ECG: Electrocardiogram: a recording of the heart's electrical activity from electrodes on the skin.
glossary.Chest X-ray: A plain radiograph of the chest showing lungs, heart size and the main vessels.
glossary.CT pulmonary angiography: A CT scan with contrast in the lung arteries, used to look for clots.
glossary.Pulmonary pressures: Pressures measured in the pulmonary artery and right heart, key to confirming pulmonary hypertension.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate test available for confirming a diagnosis.
glossary.Oxygen therapy: Giving extra oxygen through a mask or nasal tubes to correct low blood oxygen.
glossary.Diuretics: Drugs such as furosemide that make the kidneys pass more salt and water, reducing fluid overload.
glossary.Fluid overloaded: Having too much fluid in the body, causing swelling, breathlessness and raised JVP.
glossary.Hypoxic: Having too little oxygen in the blood or tissues.
glossary.Anticoagulation: Treatment with drugs that slow blood clotting, such as warfarin or a DOAC.
glossary.Lung transplantation: Surgery to replace diseased lungs with donor lungs, reserved for severe end-stage disease.
glossary.Thromboembolism: A clot that forms in one vessel and breaks off to block another.
glossary.Pulmonary emboli: Blood clots that have travelled to and lodged in the lung arteries.
glossary.Afterload: The pressure a ventricle must pump against to eject blood.
glossary.RV: Right ventricle: the heart chamber that pumps blood into the lungs.
glossary.RV hypertrophy: Thickening of the right ventricular wall from pumping against high pressure.
glossary.Dilatation: Stretching and enlargement of a chamber or vessel.
glossary.Peripheral oedema: Swelling of the legs and ankles from fluid leaking out of the veins into the tissues.
glossary.Pulmonary vasculature: The network of arteries, capillaries and veins within the lungs.
glossary.Vascular smooth muscle: Muscle in blood vessel walls that contracts to narrow the vessel and relaxes to widen it.
glossary.Vasoconstriction: Narrowing of blood vessels when the muscle in their walls contracts.
glossary.Endothelin: A powerful vessel-narrowing chemical released by the lining of blood vessels.
glossary.Epoprostenol: A prostacyclin given by continuous infusion to dilate pulmonary arteries in severe PAH.
